# Sirach Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** My child, if you are going to commit yourself to serving the Lord, brace yourself — testing will come.

**2** Steel your heart and stand firm; don't panic when disaster strikes.

**3** Hold on to him and don't let go, and you will be honored when your life is over.

**4** Take what comes your way. When circumstances humble you, be patient with them.

**5** Gold is proven in fire; those who are acceptable to God are proven in the furnace of hardship.

**6** Trust him and he will come to your aid. Walk the straight path and put your hope in him.

**7** All of you who fear the Lord — wait for his mercy, and don't wander off and stumble.

**8** All of you who fear the Lord — trust him, and you will not lose your reward.

**9** All of you who fear the Lord — hope for the best, because everlasting joy and mercy are waiting for you.

**10** Look back through the ages and think carefully: has anyone who trusted the Lord ever been put to shame? Has anyone who stayed faithful to him ever been abandoned? Has anyone who called out to him ever been ignored?

**11** The Lord is compassionate and merciful — he pardons sin and comes to the rescue when times are hard.

**12** How sad for those with cowardly hearts and limp hands — and for the double-minded person who tries to walk both roads at once.

**13** How sad for the person who gives up — he has no faith left, so he will have no shelter either.

**14** How sad for you who have run out of endurance! What will you do when the Lord comes looking for you?

**15** Those who fear the Lord take his words seriously; those who love him stay on his path.

**16** Those who fear the Lord live to please him; those who love him are soaked through with his teaching.

**17** Those who fear the Lord get their hearts ready and humble themselves before him.

**18** Better to fall into the hands of the Lord than into the hands of other people — because his mercy is as vast as his greatness.
